I can hear that you're worried about your husband, and it makes sense that you'd want answers. I can't diagnose him—schizophrenia can only be assessed by a mental health professional through direct evaluation—but I can help you think through next steps.

If you're noticing changes like hearing or seeing things others don't, strong beliefs that seem disconnected from reality, disorganized speech, or big shifts in behavior or withdrawal, those are worth discussing with a doctor. A good starting point is his primary care physician or a psychiatrist, who can rule out other causes and offer a proper assessment.

Bringing this up gently, from a place of care rather than accusation, often helps. If at any point he seems to be a danger to himself or others, please contact emergency services or a crisis line right away.

This can be frightening and lonely to navigate. Consider seeking support for yourself too—whether that's a trusted person or a counselor. You don't have to carry this alone.
